name: Corn Fritters

ingredients.name: kosher salt, plus more to taste
Neutral oil, such as vegetable oil, for frying

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, cornstarch, and baking powder until well combined; set aside.
In the bowl of a food processor, place 1 1/2 cups (255 g) corn, onion, egg, and salt. Process until a coarse puree forms, about 30 seconds, stopping to scrape down sides of bowl as needed.
Transfer pureed corn mixture to the large bowl with cornstarch mixture along with remaining 1 1/2 cups (255 g) corn kernels, and fold until just combined.

Set a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet and line with paper towels; set aside. Fill a large Dutch oven with 4 cm of oil and heat over medium-high until oil registers 175°C (350°F) with an instant-read thermometer. Working in batches of about 8 at a time, drop 1 1/2 tablespoon portions of corn batter gently into oil. Fry, stirring and flipping fritters often, until golden brown all over, 3 to 4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon or spider skimmer, transfer fritters to prepared baking sheet, and sprinkle with salt to taste. Serve immediately with maple syrup, cane syrup, or honey, if using.

description: Golden corn fritters made from fresh kernels are crisp on the outside, tender inside, and packed with the flavor of summer corn.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Maple syrup, cane syrup, or honey, for serving, optional

Notes: Fresh kernels will give the best sweetness and juiciness, but frozen corn can be used in place of fresh. Thaw, drain, and pat dry before measuring by weight (510 g; 510 g) to prevent excess moisture in the batter.

Make-ahead and storage: Corn fritters are best eaten immediately after they're fried, when they're at their crispiest.
author: Laila Ibrahim
